markdown_report:
### Insights

**Starting point.** (1) Industrial and Electronics have measured negative-win rates of 12.25% and 11.27%. These training-position results do not establish validation weakness. (2) Alignment near 0.51 means mean cosine near zero. Anti-collapse training lacks supporting evidence. (3) Feedback suggests specific-fit and recent-intent failures. Histories cannot establish ownership, compatibility or current demand.

**Related work.** (1) BERT4Rec already includes terminal-only masking [1]. The proposed intervention concerns prefix-endpoint distribution and objective weighting, with novelty conditional on baseline differences. (2) Sampled metrics can reverse comparisons [2]. Pinned validation remains authoritative. (3) CAPE motivates separating content and positional effects [3]. Perturbations cannot identify causal intent.

### Directions and framework

Prioritize integrity, reproducible supervision and controlled sensitivity.

| Layer | Existing mechanism | Gap and proposed action |
|---|---|---|
| Integrity | Mask/padding checks | Reload checkpoint and verify predictor parity [6] |
| Learning | Cloze and terminal masking [1] | Audit baseline; test explicit prefix distribution |
| Explanation | History deletion | Add position-preserving masking and random controls [3] |
| Selection | Sampled ranking [2] | Fixed macro HR@10; paired uncertainty; query log [4,5] |

### Candidate ideas

Scores are originality/potential/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each includes a benefit (+) and limitation (−).

| Idea | Originality | Potential | Difficulty |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Explicit prefix-distribution ablation** [1] | 2: + precise exposure control; − terminal masking established | 6: + falsifiable learning change; − baseline may match | 4: + sampler-focused; − weighting/accounting subtleties |
| Predictor parity certificate [6] | 3: + deployment audit; − standard testing | 6: + catches silent faults; − indirect gains | 4: + bounded fixtures; − integration |
| Position-controlled sensitivity [3] | 4: + paired controls; − established perturbations | 6: + stronger diagnosis; − no causal identification | 5: + existing hooks; − control construction |

### Selected idea: prefix terminal-mask mixture

At 10% progress, retain this small ablation, conditional on a documented baseline difference. Audit baseline endpoint/window sampling, terminal probability, truncation, mask refresh/rate/cap, corruption, zero-target handling and loss reduction before attribution.

Choose each whole batch’s branch with probability 0.5. Terminal batches sample eligible users uniformly, then endpoint t uniformly from 1,…,n−1. Input is leftpad(history[max(0,t−L+1):t]+[MASK]); supervise history[t] only. Exclude later events; retain earlier repeats. Otherwise preserve baseline Cloze sampling. Normalize loss over supervised targets within each batch, ensuring nonzero targets; this gives equal expected branch weight. Log exclusions and exposure: neither sampling nor terminal masking removes popularity shortcuts.

Keep architecture/scoring, seeds 0/42, routing, interfaces and predictor writer consistent. Use one model/checkpoint per category, single GPU, ≤200 epochs and 200 batches/epoch. Record targets, updates and GPU-seconds within the shared 43,200-second budget; equal updates need not mean equal supervision.

Preregister evaluation cadence, stopping and earliest-checkpoint tie rules. Select by pinned macro validation HR@10; report category scores and paired within-category user-bootstrap macro differences [4]. Intervals exclude training/search uncertainty [5]. Limit adaptive queries, verify reloaded predictor parity, and keep test labels untouched. Recovery remains training-exposed; compatibility and ownership remain unmodeled.

References: [1] BERT4Rec; [2] sampled-metric analysis; [3] CAPE; [4] paired bootstrap; [5] adaptive analysis; [6] checkpoint guidance. Links and limitations accompany this report.

idea.description: Test an explicitly specified training-prefix endpoint distribution and 50:50 batch-level objective mixture against the supplied corrected BERT4Rec baseline, conditional on demonstrating that its sampler differs. Train exactly one network and deploy one selected checkpoint per category.
idea.motivation: Deployment predicts from an appended mask without future context. However, BERT4Rec already describes terminal-only training samples, so terminal masking itself is not a new contribution. The falsifiable hypothesis is that changing the distribution and weighting of training-prefix endpoints improves the pinned macro validation HR@10. Existing training margins and qualitative feedback motivate investigation without establishing this mechanism or a validation gain.
idea.implementation_notes: First document the supplied baseline rather than assuming it lacks terminal supervision: user/window sampling, endpoint distribution, explicit terminal-only probability, overlapping windows, duplication, truncation order, refreshed versus fixed masks, masking rate, target cap, corruption probabilities, zero-target handling, loss family, negative proposal if applicable, and reduction. If the proposed distribution already matches it, report equivalence rather than presenting a distinct ablation. For the experimental sampler, use a dedicated RNG seeded at 42; eligible users have at least two training events, minimum context m=1, and zero-based target endpoint t is uniform on [1,n_u−1] after uniformly sampling an eligible user. Thus P(u,t)=1/[U_eligible(n_u−1)]; this is not uniform over all endpoints. Log excluded users and endpoint/item exposures. Retain the last L−1 preceding items, append reserved mask itemnum+1, and left-pad to L; the endpoint and later events are absent, but earlier occurrences of the target remain legitimate. Require L≥2. Select the branch once per entire batch with probability 0.5. Preserve the baseline loss family, negative sampling and negative reduction; normalize resulting position losses over supervised targets within each batch. Guarantee at least one target in Cloze batches. Independently normalized batches yield equal expected branch objective weight, whereas pooling mixed-branch targets would not. Do not introduce full-catalog cross-entropy or proposal changes into this sampler-only ablation. If the baseline uses sampled losses, document actual proposals, exclusions and accidental-hit handling; training sampling must not consult held-out labels. Preserve preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, architecture, initialization procedure, optimizer and evaluation cadence across comparisons; use dedicated sampler RNG streams so extra sampler draws do not perturb model RNG. Keep DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, all four category routes, single-GPU execution, at most 200 epochs and exactly 200 batches per completed epoch. Count all failures, diagnostics and training against 43,200 GPU-seconds. Record updates, target counts and elapsed GPU-seconds; label the primary comparison update-matched and report compute/supervision differences rather than claiming equal exposure. A separately preregistered target-matched comparison is optional only if feasible within the ceilings and budget. Preregister the host-supported validation cadence and stopping policy before launching; maximize four-category macro HR@10 with earliest-checkpoint ties and a bounded query count. If the host supplies only post-training validation, preregister the training endpoint instead of inventing in-training host access. Freeze the host's 200 validation users/category and 99 unique negatives/user, seed 42. Report category HR@10 and their unweighted mean. If paired per-user host outcomes are available, use 10,000 within-category paired user-bootstrap replicates with a fixed analysis seed and report the percentile 95% interval for the macro difference. Otherwise mark that interval unavailable; do not replace the evaluator. Such intervals are conditional on candidates and fitted checkpoints and exclude training-seed and adaptive-selection uncertainty. Log adaptive queries and do not inspect test labels. Preserve ModelView, item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Diagnostic batches remain (None, sequence, positive, negative), B×L, with supervised mask positions explicitly identified. Preserve model modes and RNG states during probes; return measured metrics, definitions, valid counts and unavailable reasons. Treat existing training-history sensitivity as recovery, not held-out generalization. After saving, reload the exact deployed architecture and compare item-associated scores and rankings on identical public training-prefix fixtures, auditing item mapping, routing, left padding, final-mask readout and candidate permutation. Compare validation HR@10 parity only through available host-supported evaluation. Architecture and scoring stay unchanged, but the embedded predictor writer and saved configuration must remain consistent. Deploy exactly one selected checkpoint per category; no averaging, independent score fusion or additional fitted predictors. Prefix sampling may overweight short-history users relative to endpoint-uniform sampling and may retain item-frequency shortcuts; stratify diagnostic results by history length, repeat status and training-item frequency without interpreting these as causal preferences.
idea.pseudocode:
audit_and_record_corrected_baseline_sampler_and_loss()
if proposed_sampler_matches_baseline:
    report_no_distinct_sampler_intervention()
else:
    preregister_validation_cadence_stopping_ties_and_query_limit()
    for category in fixed_four_categories:
        initialize_same_corrected_BERT4Rec_architecture(seed=42)
        sampler_rng = dedicated_rng(seed=42)
        eligible_users = users_with_at_least_two_training_events()
        assert L >= 2 and len(eligible_users) > 0
        for epoch in range(preregistered_max_epochs_at_most_200):
            for batch_index in range(200):
                terminal_branch = sampler_rng.random() < 0.5
                if terminal_branch:
                    examples = []
                    for b in range(baseline_batch_size):
                        u = uniform_choice(eligible_users, sampler_rng)
                        history = supplied_training_history[u]
                        t = sampler_rng.integers(1, len(history))
                        context = history[max(0, t-L+1):t]
                        tokens = left_pad(context + [itemnum+1], L)
                        positive = zeros(L)
                        positive[-1] = history[t]
                        examples.append((tokens, positive))
                    batch = apply_unchanged_baseline_loss_sampling(examples)
                else:
                    batch = corrected_baseline_cloze_batch_with_nonzero_targets()
                position_losses = unchanged_baseline_position_loss(model, batch)
                loss = sum(position_losses_at_supervised_positions) / number_supervised_positions
                update_same_model(loss)
                log_branch_targets_updates_and_gpu_seconds()
            apply_only_preregistered_host_supported_selection_or_stopping()
        save_one_selected_checkpoint_and_matching_predictor_configuration()
        reload_deployed_predictor_in_eval_mode()
        verify_scores_rankings_mapping_routing_and_final_mask_on_public_fixtures()

# Keep all four routes and one checkpoint/category.
# Return diagnosis metrics and definitions, distinguishing training recovery.
# Use only pinned host validation for selection; paired uncertainty requires
# available per-user host outcomes and does not correct adaptive selection.

originality.positive: Specifying endpoint probabilities, branch weighting and supervision accounting makes the experiment more precise and distinguishes potentially different exposure policies.
originality.negative: Original BERT4Rec already includes terminal-only masking. Novelty of the proposed prefix distribution is unestablished and may disappear after auditing the supplied baseline.

future_potential.positive: A controlled sampler ablation can clarify whether prefix exposure and objective weighting improve deployment-aligned ranking and guide later single-model experiments.
future_potential.negative: Benefits remain unmeasured, baseline equivalence is possible, and the intervention does not directly represent compatibility, ownership or incremental usefulness.

code_difficulty.positive: The backbone, scorer and inference architecture remain unchanged, keeping the primary implementation localized to sampling and loss accounting.
code_difficulty.negative: Correct endpoint probabilities, RNG isolation, target normalization, baseline audits, host-supported selection and deployed-predictor parity require more work than a simple branch insertion.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Introduces bidirectional sequential recommendation through masked-item prediction.
Section 3.6 explicitly describes adding samples with only the last item masked and predicts from an appended mask at inference.
limitations: Terminal-only supervision is therefore prior art, rather than a distinct contribution of this proposal.
The paper does not specify the proposed 0.5 mixing probability or establish its benefit on this benchmark.

related_work.title: Authors' BERT4Rec data generator
contributions: Provides a concrete implementation of window generation, duplicated Cloze examples and masking controls.
Illustrates why paper descriptions and implementation entry-point settings must be distinguished.
limitations: Generator defaults do not establish the supplied host baseline's settings.
Random selection of a window's final item differs from an explicit terminal-only branch and random-prefix endpoint policy.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec-VAE-Pytorch BERT dataloader
contributions: Provides an alternative dynamic masking implementation with left padding and appended-mask inference.
Demonstrates implementation variation relevant to corruption probabilities and suffix truncation.
limitations: Its sampler must not be assumed to match the corrected host baseline.
Implementation examples alone do not establish which masking distribution yields better validation ranking.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Analyzes distortions introduced by evaluating recommendation rankings with sampled candidates.
Supports restricting conclusions to the pinned candidate protocol and separating auxiliary diagnostics from selection.
limitations: Does not authorize changing the fixed host evaluator.
Repeated candidate draws do not eliminate differences between sampled and full-catalog ranking.

related_work.title: CAPE
contributions: Studies positional encoding in attention-based sequential recommendation.
Motivates controlling positional changes when interpreting history perturbations.
limitations: Does not establish that recent-history sensitivity identifies causal user intent.
Does not directly validate the proposed prefix-distribution ablation.

related_work.title: SciPy bootstrap documentation
contributions: Documents bootstrap confidence intervals and paired resampling.
Supports resampling identical user indices for both objectives within each category before recomputing their macro difference.
limitations: The proposed stratification by category and fixed-candidate interpretation are task-specific analysis choices.
User-bootstrap intervals exclude training-seed variability and adaptive checkpoint or hypothesis selection.

related_work.title: Preserving Statistical Validity in Adaptive Data Analysis
contributions: Explains how adaptive reuse of data can invalidate ordinary statistical conclusions.
Motivates preregistered hypotheses, bounded validation queries and explicit selection logs.
limitations: Logging and limiting queries do not themselves provide an adaptive-validity guarantee.
Ordinary paired bootstrap intervals do not correct winner-selection bias.

related_work.title: PyTorch: Saving and Loading Models
contributions: Documents checkpoint saving, reconstruction and evaluation-mode loading.
Supports checking the deployed predictor against the trained model after checkpoint reload.
limitations: Task-specific item mappings, category routing, mask semantics and score parity still require explicit fixtures.
Checkpoint correctness alone does not establish ranking quality.
